observations: C1-C3 pass: resolve() and _bind() pipeline works correctly for all 5 long-value patterns with UUIDs, slugs, deep paths, bearer tokens, and multi-param queries

C4 FAIL: Only 2/5 long-value patterns (P1_UUID, P4_BEARER) show parameterized using fewer tokens than literal. P3_DEEPPATH and P5_MULTIPARAM show parameterized using MORE tokens despite long concrete values. P2_SLUG is neutral (equal tokens).
C5 passes: Mean savings 15.99% across 5 long-value patterns exceeds 10% threshold, but this is driven by the two large savings patterns (UUID 44.44%, bearer 56.72%) masking the two negative patterns

C6 FAIL: Savings do NOT monotonically increase with value length. P5_MULTIPARAM (46 chars) shows -9.68% savings while P1_UUID (36 chars) shows +44.44%. Correlation r=0.3909 is well below 0.7 threshold. The relationship is non-monotonic and depends on template overhead structure, not just value length.

Root cause of C4/C6 failure: Template syntax overhead (e.g., ${orgId}, ${projectId}, ${category}, ${minPrice}, ${maxPrice}) adds tokens proportional to slot count and slot name length. Multi-slot templates with short slot names still incur fixed overhead per slot. Deep path patterns have 2 slots, multi-param have 3 slots; the per-slot overhead (varname + 3 chars ${} wrapper) is not offset by removing short numeric IDs from the URL.
C7 passes: No kernel regression; all 3 existing tests pass
C8 passes: Positive control confirms parent's short-value penalty: parameterized uses MORE tokens for 2-char numeric values (-5.26% savings), replicating the parent result

The structural breakeven point hypothesized at ~8 chars is not a clean threshold. Token savings depend on: (a) concrete value length, (b) number of parameter slots, (c) slot name length, (d) URL path structure around the values. UUIDs and bearer tokens (single-slot, long value) show strong savings; multi-slot patterns (even with long total value) show negative savings.
